text:
Cam Talbot kept Columbus in a game it had no business being in. Minnesota piled up 5.18 expected goals, a measure of the quality of its chances, against 1.37 for the Blue Jackets, and still won only 2-1. Replaying every shot over and over, the Wild would come out ahead 90 percent of the time. Talbot stopped 32 of 34 shots, 2.1 goals better than the chances he faced would normally allow.

Minnesota struck first when Danila Yurov scored at 18:12 of the opening period, with Yakov Trenin assisting. Adam Fantilli answered for CBJ exactly one minute later, tying it 1-1 on a wrist shot at 19:12, with help from Zach Werenski and Sean Monahan. That was nearly the whole of Columbus's offense on the night: the Blue Jackets managed 14 shots on goal to Minnesota's 34, and 39 shot attempts to the Wild's 66. Kirill Kaprizov broke the tie at 3:06 of the second period with a snap shot on the power play, set up by Maxim Shabanov and Joel Eriksson Ek. It proved the winner.

The pressure never let up, but neither did Talbot. Minnesota out-chanced Columbus in every period, 2.05 to 0.49 in the first, 1.63 to 0.58 in the second and 1.5 to 0.29 in the third. Yurov's best look, a 48 percent chance in the second, was stopped by Talbot. Kaprizov put five shots on goal and Matt Boldy six. Jesper Wallstedt faced only 14 shots for Minnesota and allowed one goal.
